1.pericope_label: Thus saith the Lord God; The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days; but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new moon it shall be opened. And the prince shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate without, and shall stand by the post of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship at the threshold of the gate: then he shall go forth; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening. Likewise the people of the land shall worship at the door of this gate before the Lord in the sabbaths and in the new moons. And the burnt offering that the prince shall offer unto the Lord in the sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish, and a ram without blemish. And the meat offering shall be an ephah for a ram, and the meat offering for the lambs as he shall be able to give, and an hin of oil to an ephah. And in the day of the new moon it shall be a young bullock without blemish, and six lambs, and a ram: they shall be without blemish. And he shall prepare a meat offering, an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs according as his hand shall attain unto, and an hin of oil to an ephah. And when the prince shall enter, he shall go in by the way of the porch of that gate, and he shall go forth by the way thereof.

schools.summary: Trace the prince's movements exactly and mark the limit set to them, and observe that the offerings diverge from the Mosaic law in opposite directions.
Read the eastern gate mystically as the ministry of reconciliation, and the people's worship as constant attendance on word and ordinance.
Give the plan of the chapter, note the divergence from the Mosaic proportions, and draw a political lesson from the prince's obligation to attend.
Leaves open whether rules differing from the law of Moses were ever meant to be observed, noting the later church governed itself only by the older law.

debates.question: How do these offerings stand to the Mosaic law?

positions.position: They diverge both ways: the sabbath offering is greatly increased over the law's two lambs, while the new moon's is diminished and the required sin offering omitted.
Different, as the single bullock of the new moon shows against the law's two bullocks, a ram and seven lambs.
Different in proportion generally, the prince giving according to what providence has put in his power.

outliers.claim: Doubts these rules were ever observed where they differ from the law of Moses, since the history of the later Jewish church shows it governed by that law only, this vision being treated in the next age as mystical rather than literal.

Draws a political lesson from the prince's obligation, that the chief magistrate was bound to attend public worship as much as the priest, since no man is capable of being either prince or priest who does not acknowledge God in all his ways.

9.pericope_label: But when the people of the land shall come before the Lord in the solemn feasts, he that entereth in by the way of the north gate to worship shall go out by the way of the south gate; and he that entereth by the way of the south gate shall go forth by the way of the north gate: he shall not return by the way of the gate whereby he came in, but shall go forth over against it. And the prince in the midst of them, when they go in, shall go in; and when they go forth, shall go forth. And in the feasts and in the solemnities the meat offering shall be an ephah to a bullock, and an ephah to a ram, and to the lambs as he is able to give, and an hin of oil to an ephah. Now when the prince shall prepare a voluntary burnt offering or peace offerings voluntarily unto the Lord, one shall then open him the gate that looketh toward the east, and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, as he did on the sabbath day: then he shall go forth; and after his going forth one shall shut the gate. Thou shalt daily prepare a burnt offering unto the Lord of a lamb of the first year without blemish: thou shalt prepare it every morning. And thou shalt prepare a meat offering for it every morning, the sixth part of an ephah, and the third part of an hin of oil, to temper with the fine flour; a meat offering continually by a perpetual ordinance unto the Lord. Thus shall they prepare the lamb, and the meat offering, and the oil, every morning for a continual burnt offering.

schools.summary: Explain the one-way rule as order in a vast concourse, and give the daily sacrifice's divergence from the law in both directions at once.
Read the prince among the people as Christ in the midst of his worshippers, and take the closing plural as covering all God's people.
Work out the geometry of the gates, note the entire omission of the evening offering, and suggest the rule prevented jostling.

debates.question: What does it mean that the prince is in the midst of them?

positions.position: A change of function: at the yearly feasts he need no longer represent the people, since they are present themselves, so he worships among them.
A matter of discipline: he must go straight forward like the rest, and prince and people begin and end their worship together.
A type of Christ in the midst of his worshipping people, answering to the Angel in the bush, the myrtle trees, the golden candlesticks and the tree of life.

outliers.claim: States bluntly that the evening offering is left out entirely, which makes an important difference between this and the old ordinances.

Takes the shift to the plural at the close as decisive for the whole passage, showing that not a single person is meant but all the Lord's people, who are all priests and offer spiritual sacrifices daily.

16.pericope_label: Thus saith the Lord God; If the prince give a gift unto any of his sons, the inheritance thereof shall be his sons’; it shall be their possession by inheritance. But if he give a gift of his inheritance to one of his servants, then it shall be his to the year of liberty; after it shall return to the prince: but his inheritance shall be his sons’ for them. Moreover the prince shall not take of the people’s inheritance by oppression, to thrust them out of their possession; but he shall give his sons inheritance out of his own possession: that my people be not scattered every man from his possession. After he brought me through the entry, which was at the side of the gate, into the holy chambers of the priests, which looked toward the north: and, behold, there was a place on the two sides westward. Then said he unto me, This is the place where the priests shall boil the trespass offering and the sin offering, where they shall bake the meat offering; that they bear them not out into the utter court, to sanctify the people. Then he brought me forth into the utter court, and caused me to pass by the four corners of the court; and, behold, in every corner of the court there was a court. In the four corners of the court there were courts joined of forty cubits long and thirty broad: these four corners were of one measure. And there was a row of building round about in them, round about them four, and it was made with boiling places under the rows round about. Then said he unto me, These are the places of them that boil, where the ministers of the house shall boil the sacrifice of the people.

schools.summary: Read the inheritance rule as a constitutional guard against the prince's violence and exaction, and explain why two sets of kitchens were needed.
Take the servants who are not sons for hireling ministers and carnal professors, and turn the warning against oppression into a promise about Christ.
Identify the year of liberty as the jubilee, and describe what the boiling places were used for and what came of it.
Reads the passage as a law limiting the prince's power over the crown lands, and observes that so plentiful a table at the altar needed large kitchens.

debates.question: What is the inheritance rule for?

positions.position: To keep the royal domain inalienable, since an ample territory was given precisely to prevent the prince attempting violence and exaction.
To limit the prince's power over the crown lands, allowing a deserving son a settled portion so long as it stays in the family.
To distinguish gift from inheritance, what is given to a servant reverting at the year of liberty while a son's remains his.

outliers.claim: Reports that the word rendered joined is understood by others as made with chimneys, so that the smoke of the fires and the steam of the boiling flesh might have a way to ascend, which he notes is the general rabbinic reading.

Describes what the boiling places produced, that families and friends feasted on the peace offerings brought by private devotion while portions were sent to the poor and widows and fatherless, so that the spirit of devotion preserved the spirit of mercy.
